newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Copper needs more gains to spark rally - trade.
newsitem.headline: Copper needs more gains to spark rally - trade.

text.p: Despite a post late kerb gain, more upward price movement is needed to spark a rally in copper prices, dealers in Sydney said on Thursday.
"The weight of forward selling above current levels continues to dampen efforts to rally further," LME ring dealer Mocatta Base Metals said in its latest report.
"A close above US$2,450/tonne is really what's required to reignite the bull run and that may be asking a little too much of the market at present," Mocatta said.
A lack of activity in Asia in the copper market in recent months suggests investment fund trading, mainly in London, is wielding the greatest influence on prices, another metals dealer said.
"The US$2,450 (a tonne) price level represents a premium to copper's recent high of US$2,440 in March and that's what everyone's focussing on," the dealer said.
LME copper in post kerb trading on Wednesday was indicated at US$2,427/29 a tonne versus the kerb close of US$2,414, which was down US$3.00 from the previous finish.
At 0245 GMT (12.45 p.m.), three month copper was quoted at US$2,427/32 a tonne.
